brief: A 4-entry, 8-bit FIFO for a UART receive path. Bytes must come out in the order they arrived. When the FIFO is full, new bytes are dropped rather than overwriting stored ones. Reset clears the FIFO.
note: Recorded Nemotron 3 Super interpretation (reasoning off). Read-only; run it live with your own key.

result.summary: The brief aligns with most aspects of the contract but omits details on several topics including reset kind/priority/recurrence, flag behavior specifics, and certain concurrency cases.

decisions.contract: Reset is synchronous and active-high, sampled on the rising clock edge.
decisions.note: Brief states 'Reset clears the FIFO' but does not specify if reset is synchronous/asynchronous or active-high/low.

decisions.contract: Reset wins over read and write. Occupancy becomes zero; empty is true and full is false after the edge.
decisions.note: No mention of how reset interacts with concurrent read/write operations.

decisions.contract: Reset may be asserted again at any later edge and must restore the empty state.
decisions.note: Brief does not address whether reset can be reasserted later or its effect on state.

decisions.brief_says: When the FIFO is full, new bytes are dropped rather than overwriting stored ones.
decisions.note: Matches contract: write ignored when full.

decisions.contract: Ignore the read. Nothing is consumed and nothing is bypassed.
decisions.note: Behavior on read when empty is not described in the brief.

decisions.contract: Accept both. Occupancy stays constant; the old head is read and the new word joins the tail.
decisions.note: No mention of behavior when read and write occur simultaneously at mid-occupancy.

decisions.contract: Accept only the write. The new word is not bypassed to dout.
decisions.note: No mention of behavior when read and write occur simultaneously when empty.

decisions.contract: Accept only the read. The write is ignored even though the read frees a slot.
decisions.note: No mention of behavior when read and write occur simultaneously when full.

decisions.contract: Accepted words leave exactly once and in arrival order, across pointer wraparound.
decisions.brief_says: Bytes must come out in the order they arrived.

decisions.contract: dout is registered: it holds the removed word after the edge of an accepted read (no fall-through).
decisions.note: No mention of whether dout is registered or if fall-through reads occur.

decisions.contract: DEPTH words of capacity, for the selected DEPTH.
full is true exactly when DEPTH words are stored and empty exactly when none are; there are no early-warning or almost-full semantics on these outputs.
decisions.note: No explicit statement about when full/empty flags are asserted or absence of early-warning semantics.
